paths.description: Homepage and dense category/recommendation template, highest-risk entry surface.
Primary video listing archetype with 100 thumbnail cards and pagination.
Category index archetype and mobile navigation behavior.
Representative video detail and media playback metadata surface.
Content-removal/legal support path representing a critical trust and help flow.
Arabic localized route representing internationalized templates and RTL behavior.
Representative HTTP failure state and recovery path.

findings.summary: The fixed palette does not respond to the user color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Default and dark-emulated screenshots are byte-identical at 150,560 bytes, and CSS inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule or color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme support and theme tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Motion preferences are not represented in the stylesheet
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule. Existing 0.3s to 0.8s transitions remain declared for menus and navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or shorten non-essential transitions inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Some text and controls fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a failing color-contrast audit on both the home and videos templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and background design tokens to meet WCAG contrast and verify in forced-colors.

findings.summary: Route and state changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules, while the site exposes many MPA routes and JS-toggled menu states.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for route changes and same-document transitions for state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide little state-aware orientation
findings.evidence: The home document is 13,737 CSS px tall; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress treatment, only a basic fixed scroll-to-top link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment.

findings.summary: Dropdowns use manually positioned absolute layouts
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS positions language, category, and sorting dropdowns with absolute left/right offsets and contains no anchor positioning or fallback positions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for transient menus.

findings.summary: Navigation changes do not cue the destination
findings.evidence: The route inventory and CSS show ordinary links and abrupt state toggles, with no highlight, directional transition, or focus cue after navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve focus and add restrained directional or highlight cues for route and in-page changes.

findings.summary: A third-party age gate obscures every audited content page on load
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the whole page blurred beneath a non-dismissible AgeVerif prompt before any interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep required age assurance content-first: explain the process, offer privacy and exit choices, use an accessible modal, and avoid loading unrelated ads first.

findings.summary: The age gate is an opaque custom element rather than an accessible dialog
findings.evidence: DOM queries found no dialog or role=dialog. Hit testing returned a closed AGEVERIF-CHECKER custom element, and Lighthouse reported a malformed accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the gate with a native dialog or equivalent exposed semantics, focus trapping, labelled controls, and an explicit exit.

findings.summary: Dense tags, partner promotions, and the gate crowd out primary content
findings.evidence: The home page renders 13,737 CSS px of categories and recommended-site chrome, while the first viewport is entirely occupied by the age gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated category and partner blocks, prioritize primary content, and defer secondary promotions.

findings.summary: Reusable cards only respond to global viewport breakpoints
findings.evidence: CSS inspection shows many viewport media queries and no @container rule, although card variants are reused at multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card and navigation components containment and container-query adaptations.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the search input and button with outline-style none; several nav targets are about 29 to 33 CSS px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible styles and make primary interactive targets at least 44 by 44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: The first viewport does not explain the site or content choice
findings.evidence: Every main template opens on a generic AgeVerif prompt over blurred content, so users cannot evaluate the page purpose before pressing Start.
findings.suggestedFix: Explain the site purpose and age-check consequences in the gate, with clear continue and leave actions.

findings.summary: The primary content flow depends on an inaccessible third-party gate
findings.evidence: The visible flow stops at a closed-shadow AgeVerif element; agent and DOM probes cannot identify or activate its Start control, and Lighthouse says the accessibility tree is malformed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace or configure the gate so its controls are in the accessibility tree and the continue path works predictably for keyboard and assistive technology users.

findings.summary: The gate offers no visible cancel, leave, privacy, or recovery path
findings.evidence: Screenshots show only a Start action and generic copy. No alternative or recovery control is visible on desktop or mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear leave, privacy, help, and retry states, and preserve context if verification fails.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on primary templates
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP at 4.8s on home and 5.8s on videos, both above the 2.5s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce initial image volume and redirects, and defer below-fold content.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is heavy and includes a redirect loop
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 160 requests and 2.77 MB, uncompressed HTML/CSS/JS, render-blocking resources, and HTTP to HTTPS to HTTP 307 redirects.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve one canonical HTTPS response, compress text, shorten blocking chains, and apply useful cache and priority hints.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 21 to 22 KiB unused CSS and 37 to 76 KiB unused JavaScript across home and videos.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific assets and load third-party scripts only when required.

findings.summary: Search and gate controls lack reliable accessible names and semantics
findings.evidence: The search input has no associated label, the custom age gate exposes no dialog semantics, and Lighthouse failed the label and accessibility-tree audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the search field, expose gate controls through native semantics, and verify names and roles with axe or Lighthouse.

findings.summary: Text and UI contrast is insufficient
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit on both home and videos.
findings.suggestedFix: Update color tokens to meet WCAG AA in default and high-contrast conditions.

findings.summary: Heading, navigation, and focus structure is weak
findings.evidence: All main templates have zero h1 elements; the home page has no nav landmark, and search controls suppress focus outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1 per page, semantic nav landmarks, and visible focus styles in logical DOM order.

findings.summary: The removal page is not legible on mobile
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshot renders the removal instructions as extremely small centered text occupying only a narrow strip at the top.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a readable base font, constrained line length, left-aligned prose, and fluid spacing.

findings.summary: Small targets and uncaptained video reduce inclusive access
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured multiple nav/search targets below 44 CSS px high; the detail probe found video elements with zero caption tracks.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target sizes, retain zoom and reflow support, and add captions or equivalent transcripts to meaningful media.

findings.summary: Browser errors are logged during load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console on both the home and videos templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve each runtime and network console error and prevent expected third-party failures from surfacing as uncaught errors.

findings.summary: Image and document asset hygiene is poor
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 100 video thumbnails missing width/height and srcset, all in legacy JPEG, and 96 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add dimensions, responsive sources, modern formats, and lazy loading while preserving useful alt text.

findings.summary: DevTools reports browser-platform issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed inspector-issues on both templates, and the HAR recorded an aborted statistics request plus a favicon 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Clear DevTools issues, remove broken requests, and keep third-party integration failures contained.

findings.summary: Canonical and indexing signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: No canonical link is present, /sitemap.xml returns a 404 page, Lighthouse reports invalid hreflang, and transport redirects loop between HTTP and HTTPS.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose a canonical HTTPS origin, emit canonical and valid hreflang links, publish a sitemap, and align robots and redirects.

findings.summary: Detail pages lack entity and social metadata
findings.evidence: The representative detail page has no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite representing a video entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD plus Open Graph and social preview metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: The site is served over HTTP without baseline security headers
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports HTTP, no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; all six cookies lack Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve exclusively over HTTPS, fix redirects, secure cookies, and deploy a restrictive CSP plus baseline security headers.

findings.summary: Third parties and persistent identifiers load before meaningful consent
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw five third-party origins including age verification and ad infrastructure; a 400-day __suvt cookie and SameSite=None cookies are set on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent third parties, document purpose and retention, shorten identifiers, and defer advertising until an appropriate lawful choice.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS, clickjacking protection, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, nosniff, a strict referrer policy, and a minimal permissions policy.

findings.summary: Critical UI relies on opaque third-party runtime behavior
findings.evidence: The gate is a closed custom element and its statistics request aborts; menus use manually positioned absolute dropdowns without modern fallback positioning.
findings.suggestedFix: Use accessible first-party fallback UI and resilient overlay positioning so third-party failure cannot block the page.

findings.summary: HTTP failures fall through to a bare server page
findings.evidence: A representative missing URL displays only “404 Not Found nginx” with no navigation, search, explanation, or recovery link.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide branded 404 and network error states with useful navigation, retry, and search options.

findings.summary: The Arabic variant lacks RTL direction and relies on physical layout properties
findings.evidence: The Arabic page declares lang=ar but no dir, while CSS inspection counted 46 physical left/right rules and only 10 logical-property rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl for Arabic and migrate layout to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: Localized pages do not localize numeric presentation
findings.evidence: The Arabic route translates labels but displays category counts with the same Western formatting as English and exposes no evidence of locale-aware number formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Format counts and other locale-sensitive data with Intl.NumberFormat for the active locale.

findings.summary: The age gate asks users to start a third-party process without meaningful context or choice
findings.evidence: The gate loads with only Start, no leave option, no privacy link, no provider explanation, while advertising and age-verification requests already run.
findings.suggestedFix: Present honest purpose, provider, data-use, continue and leave choices before third-party processing.

findings.summary: Thumbnail delivery wastes bandwidth
findings.evidence: All 100 inspected thumbnails are JPEG with no srcset; all lack dimensions, and Lighthouse estimates 588 to 815 KiB of image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources, set dimensions, and prioritize only visible images.

findings.summary: Nearly all below-fold thumbnails load eagerly
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 96 below-fold thumbnails without loading=lazy; the home HAR fetched 148 images and 2.53 MB of image transfers.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, paginate or virtualize long lists, and stop background requests that add no immediate value.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is disproportionate to the first interaction
findings.evidence: The HAR reports 129 third-party requests and 2.28 MB classified third-party, while the only visible first interaction is an age gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Budget third-party scripts and media, defer advertising, and cache or eliminate low-value requests.

Use RTL direction and logical CSS on localized routes
Add resilient branded failure and fallback states
